“Don't you miss having a strong man's shoulder to lean on?” asked Rebecca223, for a hundred dollars. “Would you quit your business if you met the love of your life?”

Freya decided to answer.

“Business won't replace a husband, and a husband won't replace your life's work. Though business doesn't need to be pleased the way a lover does. And good business *always* stands by you,” here Freya smiled, “which, you'll agree, sets it apart from a husband, and favorably.”

The chats exploded. The Twitter and Instagram feeds on the side monitors raced like mad. The feminist community mobilized in full force, and the feed suddenly blossomed with rainbow-haired avatars, like an exotic greenhouse. Now it wasn't just the assistants but Freya's own fans who were filing reports and slinging mud at the right-wingers who had flocked to the light of her stream from their anonymous loser forums. There had always been a lot of trouble with right-wingers.

And yet three hundred and eighty... no, three hundred and ninety thousand live viewers remained three hundred and ninety thousand live viewers. No matter how they smelled.

Trolls tried to flood the broadcast with questions like “Do you shave your face?” and “Try shaving your legs”: no imagination, but sheer numbers. Dim-witted sad green frogs started popping up in the chat. Freya kept smiling and answering selected questions, glancing at the chat where her assistants were. Whichever way you looked at it, the comments set the tone. Still, the moderators' help turned out not to be needed.

The trolls' mothers wouldn't give them more than five dollars for school lunch. So they were utterly crushed by a counterattack from the very core of Freya's audience, rallied by calls from fan groups on Twitter, TikTok, and Instagram. Moms on maternity leave, manicurists, and students from the provinces rushed to rescue their idol. Housewives who had traded their ladles for enormous smartphones at the loud call of the modern economy. And also men who wanted the attention of all the women mentioned above, and so posed as “one of their own,” not even noticing how they were burning twenty bucks a month, and often more, on Freya.

Not the best audience if you're a serious woman sharing secrets of *true* success, but a devoted one. And devotion counts for a lot in real business.

Right before Freya's eyes, the haters' comments were drowned out by twenty- and fifty-dollar messages: “Go, Freya!”, “Freya, we love you!”, “#AxelsenSexuals!” The stakes rose quickly, and soon donations under ten dollars didn't even appear on screen. Finally the girl smiled sincerely.
